structured_output.what_is_happening: "Merry Chrismas" (misspelled, and launched in September) is a pump.fun token that shows as launched and migrated to PumpSwap at the same second. It is about 19 minutes old. GMGN puts the ATH price at 0.00076, roughly a $760k market cap. By detection the price had collapsed about 85% in 5 minutes to about $87k. The snapshot 4 seconds later shows about $167k, a bounce of about 90% from the trigger price. Roughly 2,160 unique buyers and 2,119 unique sellers traded close to 10k transactions in about 30 minutes, on about $36k of liquidity. The token has no socials apart from a GeckoTerminal "twitter" field pointing at an old X status ID, apparently from around December 2025. There is also a copycat with the same name and zero liquidity.

narrative.description: A generic seasonal 'Christmas' meme that is out of season and misspelled. It seems to piggyback on one old X post. There is no project site, no community links and no stated story.
narrative.why_spreading: The activity looks like a fast launch pump to about $760k followed by a dump. Buyer and seller counts are almost identical, which points to momentum and bot trading rather than a story people are spreading.

token_connection.why_this_token: It was launched first and holds essentially all the volume and liquidity for this name. The one competitor was created about 4 minutes later and has zero liquidity.
token_connection.competing_tokens: 7LJD...BAGS (CHRISMAS, Merry Chrismas): $0 liquidity, about $10 of volume in the last hour. It is effectively dead.

authenticity.evidence: Holders are very widely spread: top 10 hold 1.4%, dev holds 0.04%, there are only 2 bundlers, 21 fresh wallets and 1 sniper, and GMGN shows a 0% bot/degen rate. Against that, 'top_entrapment_trader_pct' is 0.78. Unique buyers and sellers are nearly equal at about 2.1k each over 30 minutes. The chart is a textbook pump from launch to about $760k and then an 85% dump within minutes. No paid boosts and no DexScreener profile.
authenticity.uncertainty: I can't see who drove the spike and the dump. The high entrapment share and symmetric buy/sell flow could be volume bots or a coordinated exit.

structural_risks: Price already fell about 80% from its ATH, which leaves a large overhang of trapped buyers who will sell into any bounce
Liquidity of about $36k at a $167k market cap means violent swings either way
Buy and sell flow looks bot-like and symmetric
No socials or community to support a second leg
Launch and migration have the same timestamp, which is unusual

structured_output.counterargument: The coin has already shown it can reach about $760k, and it is spread across more than 2.5k holders with no dev supply and LP 100% burned, so a clean rug is unlikely. Pump.fun coins that dump 85% and then hold their volume often bounce 2 to 3 times. A move from about $167k to about $334k would only retrace about 40% of the dump, so +100% is within this coin's shown volatility.
unknowns: The actual entry price at T1+4m, given the jump from $87k to $167k within seconds
Who sold at the top, and whether those wallets are gone
Whether the old X status has any real viral pull
Whether the volume comes from bots

structured_output.thesis: This is a coin that pumped hard and then dumped, and it is now dead-cat bouncing in extreme volatility. Structure is clean (authorities renounced, LP burned, holders spread out), so the risk of a liquidity pull is moderate rather than high. But there is no narrative, a trapped-buyer overhang and bot-like flow, so the stop at -50% is more likely to hit than the +100% target. Its volatility gives it a slightly better than average runner chance, but that is not strong.
